records.real_world_identity_notes: The RaceRoom Tatuus F4 observation is best identified as the first-generation Tatuus F4-T014 FIA Formula 4 chassis introduced in 2014. RaceRoom's F4 Cup label is simulator context, not a separate real-world model. Tatuus distinguishes the later second-generation T-421 from the T-014, and championship-specific engine or electronics packages should not be silently generalized beyond the evidence reviewed.
records.confidence_basis: Tatuus identifies the T-014 as its 2014 Formula 4 car and names the later T-421 as its second-generation successor. FIA Technical List No.53 identifies the exact homologated chassis as Tatuus FIA F4 T014 and pairs it with the Sadev SL75LW-F4 gearbox. RaceRoom's official store independently names the simulator car Tatuus F4 and gives the year as 2014. No matching Tatuus record is present in the checked-out curated dataset, so this is a new record proposal.

records.specification_basis: The T014 technical outline explicitly specifies an LCD display integrated into the steering wheel, and the exact-model cockpit photograph visibly shows a central digital display on the wheel. The reviewed exact-model photograph shows a fixed-grip control-face wheel rather than a conventional round or D-shaped rim. Under the record vocabulary, open-top is not applicable to the gt-formula construction. The clear Tatuus F4 cockpit photograph shows fixed molded left/right grips with a control face between them, matching the database definition of gt-formula. GB4 explicitly describes the Tatuus F4-T014 as having a six-speed gearbox, and the T014 technical outline independently says Sadev six-speed gearbox. The FIA list identifies the homologated Sadev SL75LW-F4 for the T014, while the T014 technical descriptions explicitly call the transmission sequential. The exact T014 specifications explicitly state paddle shift/paddleshift, and the cockpit photograph visibly shows paddle shifters. Both exact T014 technical descriptions call the gearbox sequential. No H-gate first-gear position is inferred from the paddle hardware. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/standing_start_clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift.
